system: common law system; has nonbinding judicial review of Acts of Parliament under the Human Rights Act of 1998

constitution.history: uncoded; partly statutes, partly common law and practice
constitution.amend: proposed as a bill for an Act of Parliament by the government, by the House of Commons, or by the House of Lords; passage requires agreement by both houses and by the monarch (Royal Assent)

courts.highest: Supreme Court (consists of 12 justices, including the court president and deputy president)
courts.judges: judge candidates selected by an independent committee of several judicial commissions, then recommended to the prime minister, and appointed by the monarch; justices serve for life
courts.lower: England and Wales: Court of Appeal (civil and criminal divisions); High Court; Crown Court; County Courts; Magistrates' Courts; Scotland: Court of Sessions; Sheriff Courts; High Court of Justiciary; tribunals; Northern Ireland: Court of Appeal in Northern Ireland; High Court; county courts; magistrates' courts; specialized tribunals

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of the United Kingdom

world: accepts compulsory ICJ jurisdiction with reservations; accepts ICCt jurisdiction

gov.type: parliamentary constitutional monarchy; a Commonwealth realm

executive.chosen: the monarchy is hereditary; following legislative elections, the leader of the majority party or majority coalition usually becomes the prime minister
executive.cabinet: Cabinet appointed by the prime minister
